title: 19.8 A 0.65V-VDD 10.4-to-11.8GHz Fractional-N Sampling PLL Achieving 73.8fsrms Jitter, -271.5dB FoMN, and -61 dBc in-Band Fractional Spur in 40nm CMOS
problem: Sub-0.7V ultra-low-voltage PLLs must achieve sub-100fs fractional-N performance, but existing DTC and DAC approaches face voltage-headroom limitations, nonlinearity, and noise folding at low supplies.
motivation: Digital-centric SoCs at sub-0.7V supply require low-jitter fractional-N PLLs for high-speed wireless transceivers, but voltage headroom constraints severely degrade phase noise and modulation performance.
method: This is a fractional-N sampling PLL (a frequency-locking circuit that divides by fractional amounts and measures phase at specific moments) designed to operate at 0.65V. It uses a two-stage converter approach: a coarse digital-to-time converter paired with a fine resistor-based DAC, allowing precise frequency tuning across a wide range. The circuit applies hybrid cascaded digital predistortion—a technique where it inverts the hardware's own distortion patterns in two stages—to cancel out nonlinearity from both the timing converter and the phase detector. The phase detector uses a negative-level-inverter topology, a specialized circuit design that reduces noise specifically at low voltages where power supply headroom is limited.
key_novelty: Combining hybrid cascaded digital predistortion (which cancels hardware distortion to reduce correction overhead and minimize noise folding) with a negative-level-inverter phase detector (designed to operate with minimal voltage headroom) enables the fractional-N sampling PLL to achieve 73.8fs jitter at 0.65V supply voltage.
contributions: Hybrid cascaded DPD reducing hardware overhead vs conventional DPD
Extended TSPC and TSPC multi-modulus divider supporting 10.4-11.8GHz operation
primary_theme: ultra-low-voltage fractional-N sampling PLL with smart predistortion
